title: Factory state machines
description: Single source of truth for the legal state transitions of Job, StageRun, Attempt and TaskNode. docs/architecture/state-machine.md renders its tables from this file. The domain crate must accept exactly the (from, event) pairs listed here and reject every other pair.

actors.engine: The workflow use-case layer. The only component that writes a status, always inside one database transaction. Every transition in this file is applied by the engine; the actor column only says who may request it.
actors.worker: A process that holds an attempt lease. May request transitions for its own attempt only, and only with the current lease epoch.
actors.sweeper: The timer tick inside the engine. Acts on deadlines, lease expiry and retry back-off.
actors.gate: The deterministic gate evaluator called by the engine while a stage run is GATING. Reads evidence, never agent prose.
actors.requester: The human who submitted the request. Must appear on the tenant's named requester allowlist in protected configuration. Holding a GitHub role is not enough.
actors.operator: A human with operational rights on the tenant: pause, resume, cancel, unblock, grant budget.
actors.approver: A human with the approval role defined by the tenant approval policy.
actors.security_approver: A human on the explicit security approver list kept in protected central configuration. Required to dispose of a security-class block. Matches the role of the same name in policies/approval.yaml.
actors.org_admin: A human organization administrator. May raise a budget above its ceiling, raise autonomy, and enable anything that is off by default. Matches policies/approval.yaml.

guards.G_ADMISSION_OK: The requester is on the tenant's named requester allowlist in protected configuration, the tenant is within its job quota, the repository is registered and enabled, the repository passed the protection preflight (otherwise the job may only run at autonomy level L0), policy allows this class of request, and neither the repository nor the organization has reached a ceiling of its day (budgets.hard_ceilings.per_repo_day and per_org_day).
guards.G_ADMISSION_DENIED: The requester is not on the allowlist, the quota is exceeded, the repository is not registered or is disabled, policy forbids this class of request, or the repository or the organization has reached a ceiling of its day or its usage could not be read. The reason is recorded and no reply reveals which test failed.
guards.G_ANY_STAGE_WAITING: At least one stage run of the job is WAITING_FOR_HUMAN.
guards.G_NO_STAGE_WAITING: No stage run of the job is WAITING_FOR_HUMAN.
guards.G_ACTOR_MAY_PAUSE: The principal holds the operator role on the tenant.
guards.G_ANY_STAGE_BLOCKED: At least one stage run of the job is BLOCKED.
guards.G_BLOCK_DISPOSITIONS_RECORDED: Every BLOCKED stage run has a recorded disposition: capability re-probe passed, or an allowed override, or a rework decision.
guards.G_ACTOR_MAY_CANCEL: The principal is the requester of the job or holds the operator role.
guards.G_ALL_ATTEMPTS_TERMINAL: Every attempt of the job is in a terminal state and every sandbox has been torn down or flagged as leaked.
guards.G_UNRECOVERABLE: The newest run of a stage kind in the job's scope is FAILED (by S06, S12 or S16), no newer run replaces it, and no rework route or retry budget remains; or a job-level hard limit was reached under a policy that says fail. The engine builds the facts from the listing of the job's stage runs, so a rework that created a newer run first leaves the guard unmet.
guards.G_REJECTION_RECORDED: The intake decision is decline, or an authorized approver recorded a reject decision.
guards.G_PIPELINE_SCOPE_COMPLETE: Every stage kind in the job's configured scope has a run that is PASSED, or SKIPPED because a recorded rule says the stage does not apply, and that run is not superseded; the approval decision is approve; and the evidence ledger hash chain verifies.
guards.G_UPSTREAM_PASSED: Every required upstream stage run is PASSED, or SKIPPED because a recorded rule says the stage does not apply, and is not superseded. Every consumed artifact hash equals the current version (a skipped stage produced none, and the stage contract records the skip rule instead of a hash). The stage contract resolved and validated against its schema.
guards.G_NOT_APPLICABLE_DECIDED: A deterministic rule, a domain profile or a policy states that the stage does not apply. The rule and its inputs are recorded in the ledger. An agent opinion is never sufficient.
guards.G_LEASE_ACQUIRED: The stage run is READY at the version the claim read, the job is ACTIVE, not_before has passed by the database clock, the concurrency quota allows it, and the runtime capability check passed. The store makes the check and the move one atomic step (start_attempt), so two workers cannot both pass it.
guards.G_OUTPUT_SCHEMA_VALID: The attempt succeeded and its output validates against the stage outputs schema, and the output artifact hash is stored.
guards.G_RETRY_ALLOWED: The failure class is retryable under the stage contract, the attempts used since the last human answer are below max_attempts, the budget has room for another attempt, and, after INVALID_OUTPUT, no more than two repairs have been made (a repair is a retry that follows an invalid-output failure; the cap comes from policy and can only be lowered).
guards.G_FAILURE_NONRETRYABLE: Retrying cannot help: the failure class is POLICY_DENIED or INTERNAL, or the stage contract does not list it in retry_on. BUDGET_EXHAUSTED is not covered here, because a budget limit asks a human (S07). Reaching the attempt limit is not covered either, because an attempt limit asks a human (S07).
guards.G_ESCALATION_REQUIRED: A budget limit was hit (the failure class is BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, or a retry would be allowed in every other way but the budget has no room), the attempt limit or the repair cap was reached on a failure class the stage contract lists as retryable, the agent returned a structured needs_human request, the stagnation detector fired, or policy requires a human decision here.
guards.G_GATE_PASS_EVIDENCED: The gate decision is PASS and is persisted, every acceptance criterion of the stage contract has a ledger entry, and every mandatory gate report is PASSED or NOT_APPLICABLE with a recorded reason. No gate report is BLOCKED.
guards.G_REWORK_ALLOWED: The verdict is CHANGES_REQUIRED or a deterministic gate FAILED, the rework rounds used on the count of the target stage are below its cap of two, the failing set differs from the previous round, and budget remains. The specification (SPECIFICATION), the design (ARCHITECTURE and TASK_PLANNING), the code (IMPLEMENTATION) and the documentation (DOCUMENTING) each have their own count, so rounds on one never use the rounds of another (ADR 0023). After the second round on a count a human decides.
guards.G_NEEDS_HUMAN_VERDICT: The verdict is NEEDS_HUMAN, or the rework limit, the stagnation detector or a budget limit was reached, or the gate itself is a human gate, or a finding that justifies the verdict has a defect class that only a person can decide (specification, or policy; see defect_routing).
guards.G_BLOCKING_CONDITION: The verdict is BLOCK, a mandatory gate could not run (tool unavailable or probe failed), or a deterministic check detected a policy violation. A reviewer's finding with defect class policy asks a person instead (S10).
guards.G_GATE_FAILED_NO_REWORK: The gate FAILED and the stage has no rework route, for example an intake record that is still invalid after bounded repair.
guards.G_ANSWER_RECORDED: A human answer, clarification, approval of residual input or budget extension is recorded with the principal and becomes a new input hash for the stage. It also starts a new attempt window: attempts and repairs are counted from the answer. A budget extension that raises a ceiling is accepted only from an org_admin.
guards.G_APPROVER_AUTHORIZED: The decision is approve, the principal holds the role the approval policy requires for this stage and risk tier, the evidence digest the human saw equals the current evidence digest, and every warning of the rule translation-unfaithful in the gate reports of that evidence has a recorded human decision.
guards.G_HUMAN_REWORK_ALLOWED: The principal holds the approver or operator role and the rework rounds used on the count of the target the person names are below its cap of two (the four counts of G_REWORK_ALLOWED). The stagnation detector does not apply to human requests. After the second round on a count a human must choose to continue, with the decision recorded.
guards.G_HUMAN_REJECTED: An authorized approver recorded a reject decision with a reason.
guards.G_BLOCK_CLEARED_RERUN: The capability re-probe passed, or the missing dependency is now available, or a person recorded the decision on a dependency that the blocked stage run was waiting for (add_new_direct_dependency, or approve_build_code for build code), after the attempt that blocked it, bound to the exact name, version and checksum in the evidence that run stored. The engine reads the third alternative from what it stored, and the caller does not assert it. The stage can run again.
guards.G_OVERRIDE_PERMITTED: Policy permits an override for this block code, the principal holds the required role (security_approver for security-class blocks), a justification is recorded, and the blocked gate is not a mandatory gate of an active domain profile. The engine reads the gate and the code of each block from the event it stored when the stage run blocked, and holds back a block that its configuration lists (gate_integrity.non_overridable_blocks) whatever facts the caller gives; the caller's facts can only narrow what the engine allows. An override records accepted residual risk. It never creates an assurance level claim.
guards.G_NO_ACTIVE_ATTEMPT: The stage run has no attempt in STARTING, RUNNING or CANCELLING.
guards.G_UPSTREAM_INVALIDATED: A consumed upstream artifact was superseded by a newer version, an upstream stage run was reworked, or an external change listed in the invalidation table happened (the source request was edited after the intake snapshot, or a value bound to gate evidence changed).
guards.G_SANDBOX_PROVISIONED: The sandbox provider returned a session for this attempt, which means it created the container, read its posture back, found every part equal to the spec and the policy, started it and passed the runtime self-check. The tool grants that policy approved are recorded in the audit log, the runtime probe of this attempt supports every capability the stage needs, and the lease epoch is current.
guards.G_LEASE_EPOCH_CURRENT: The epoch sent by the worker equals the stored epoch and now is not past lease_expires_at.
guards.G_EPOCH_CURRENT: The epoch sent by the worker equals the stored epoch.
guards.G_DEADLINE_PASSED: Now is past the attempt deadline.
guards.G_LEASE_EXPIRED: Now is past lease_expires_at and no heartbeat arrived.
guards.G_CANCEL_ALLOWED: The attempt is not terminal and the job is CANCELLING or the stage run is being superseded.
guards.G_SANDBOX_GONE: The sandbox no longer exists, confirmed by the sandbox provider.
guards.G_TEARDOWN_DEADLINE_PASSED: The teardown grace period elapsed. The sandbox is force-killed and a leaked_resources alert is raised if it cannot be confirmed gone.
guards.G_TASK_DEPS_SUCCEEDED: Every task this node depends on is SUCCEEDED.
guards.G_TASK_STARTED_BY_ATTEMPT: The IMPLEMENTATION attempt picked this task as the next one in topological order.
guards.G_TASK_EVIDENCE_RECORDED: A commit exists for the task, changed paths are inside the task's owned files, no protected path changed, and the per-task checks passed.
guards.G_TASK_RETRY_ALLOWED: The task retry count is below the per-task limit and the stage budget has room.
guards.G_ENVIRONMENT_BLOCKED: The attempt ended because something the stage cannot work without is missing or unsafe, not because the work failed: the container runtime is unreachable, the image is not on the host, the posture check found a difference, the spec was weaker than the policy, a required tool or runtime capability is absent, or the policy file could not be loaded. The cause is recorded. Retrying with the same settings cannot help, and trying other settings is forbidden.
guards.G_REAUTHORIZATION_REQUIRED: The stage run is an INTAKE run created after an external change to the source request, and the hash of the current original request differs from the hash the requester authorized; or policy asks the requester to confirm before any agent reads the text. No attempt starts and no agent reads the new text until a person answers.

job.title: Job
job.description: Lifecycle of one request. Says whether the factory is still working on it, not how far the work has been verified. Verification maturity is tracked separately as assurance levels.

RECEIVED.meaning: The request passed authorization at the API boundary and is stored. Not yet admitted.

ACTIVE.meaning: Stage runs are being scheduled and executed.

WAITING_FOR_HUMAN.meaning: At least one stage run needs a human answer, decision or approval.

PAUSED.meaning: An operator paused the job. No new attempt is leased. Running attempts finish or time out.

BLOCKED.meaning: A stage run cannot proceed or be promoted without an explicit disposition.

CANCELLING.meaning: Cancellation was requested. Attempts and sandboxes are being torn down.

COMPLETED.meaning: Every stage in the job's configured scope passed and the approval decision is recorded. This does not mean merged, released or deployed, and it says nothing about verification maturity.

FAILED.meaning: The job cannot continue and no rework route or budget remains.

CANCELLED.meaning: Cancelled by an authorized human and fully torn down.

REJECTED.meaning: Refused at admission, declined at intake, or rejected by an approver.

effects: create the INTAKE stage run in PENDING
record the denial reason
notify the requester and approvers
stop leasing new attempts
engine re-evaluates J03 and J07 immediately
notify operators
request cancel on every non-terminal attempt
mark non-terminal stage runs CANCELLED
record the failing stage run and reason
tear down any sandbox
write the final evidence manifest hash

stage_run.title: Stage run
stage_run.description: One execution of one stage kind for a job. Terminal runs are immutable. Rework creates a new run; it never reopens an old one. When more than one of S05, S06 and S07 is legal for a failed attempt, the engine takes the first that applies in this order: S07 for BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, S05 when a retry is allowed, S06 when the class is not retryable, otherwise S07 because the attempt limit, the repair cap or the budget stopped a retry.

PENDING.meaning: Created. Upstream requirements are not met yet.

READY.meaning: Schedulable. Needs an attempt. Also the state during retry back-off, with not_before in the future.

GATING.meaning: Work is done. The deterministic gate or independent evaluator is deciding. Success claimed by an agent has no effect here.

WAITING_FOR_HUMAN.meaning: Needs a human answer, budget decision, gate decision or approval.

BLOCKED.meaning: Cannot proceed or be promoted. Needs a recorded disposition.

PASSED.meaning: The gate decision is PASS with evidence. Settled, but becomes SUPERSEDED if its inputs are invalidated.

REWORK_REQUESTED.meaning: The gate sent the work back. A new run of the route target stage replaces this one.

FAILED.meaning: Retries or rework exhausted, or the failure is not retryable, or a human rejected.

SKIPPED.meaning: NOT_APPLICABLE by deterministic rule, profile or policy, with the rule recorded. Counts as satisfied for the stages that require it and for completion, never as passed, and never as evidence for an assurance level. Becomes SUPERSEDED when an input of the decision changes.

SUPERSEDED.meaning: Replaced because an upstream input changed.

append a ledger entry with the rule and inputs

supersede downstream runs

record the block code and, for each gate report that is BLOCKED, the gate and the code of its block in the event payload (blocks), which an override reads back
new input hash recorded
next attempt receives the answer as untrusted-but-authorized input
append a ledger entry of kind expert_judgment with the approver identity
create a new run of the route target stage with the human instructions as input

append invalidating ledger entries for this run

record the block code and a BLOCKED gate report as evidence
never try another sandbox profile or other settings

no attempt is created and no agent reads the new text

attempt.title: Attempt
attempt.description: One try at a stage run, owned by one worker through one lease. The attempt is created together with its lease, so there is no pre-lease state.

STARTING.meaning: Lease acquired. Sandbox and agent runtime are being prepared.

RUNNING.meaning: The agent or tool is executing and the worker is heartbeating.

CANCELLING.meaning: Cancel requested. Teardown in progress. Reports are kept for audit and cannot change the outcome.

SUCCEEDED.meaning: Output received, validated against the outputs schema and stored. Says nothing about quality; the gate decides that.

FAILED.meaning: Ended with a failure class: TOOL_ERROR, INVALID_OUTPUT, BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, POLICY_DENIED, PROVIDER_ERROR, SANDBOX_ERROR or INTERNAL.

TIMED_OUT.meaning: The attempt deadline passed. The sandbox is killed.

LEASE_LOST.meaning: The lease expired without heartbeat. The worker is presumed dead. Its later writes are rejected by the lease epoch.

CANCELLED.meaning: Torn down after a cancel request.

effects: record the sandbox id, image digest and runtime capability record
failure class SANDBOX_ERROR
extend lease_expires_at
no domain event; metrics only
store the output artifact
engine validates the output; invalid output takes A05 instead
record the failure class
request sandbox kill
increment lease_epoch to fence the old worker
best-effort sandbox teardown
signal the worker
start the teardown grace period
force kill
raise a leaked_resources alert when removal cannot be confirmed

task_node.title: Task node (Slice 1 minimal)
task_node.description: Status of one node of the task DAG. In Slice 1 the DAG runs sequentially inside a single IMPLEMENTATION attempt, so task nodes are bookkeeping for resume and evidence, not independently leased work. Slice 3 replaces this with independently leased work items and supersedes this section.

READY.meaning: All dependencies succeeded. Next in topological order.

RUNNING.meaning: The IMPLEMENTATION attempt is working on it.

SUCCEEDED.meaning: A commit exists and the per-task checks passed.

FAILED.meaning: The attempt could not complete this task. Can be retried.

effects: append a ledger entry with the commit and the checks
the next attempt resumes from the first task that is not SUCCEEDED

pipeline.description: Stage kinds in execution order. A stage gate is the GATING phase of its own stage run; gates are not separate stages. requires lists the stage kinds whose PASSED, non-superseded run must exist before this stage can leave PENDING.

stages.gate: deterministic checks on the normalized request plus bounded repair; human clarification when ambiguity is material
reproducible repository map and a build and test baseline run in a sandbox
deterministic specification gate plus independent specification reviewer; freezes the SpecificationContract
profile resolution and tool capability probes; BLOCKED when a mandatory profile gate cannot run
schema validation, requirement-to-design traceability coverage, independent critic when risk tier is high or a design decision needs a person
deterministic DAG validator: acyclic, every acceptance criterion covered, owned files do not overlap, sizes bounded
scope check: changed paths inside owned files, no protected path touched, no test weakening
trusted gate definitions from the protected base branch; format, lint, build, tests, secret scan, acceptance evidence mapping
ReviewVerdict from a reviewer that receives the frozen spec, the diff and verified gate evidence, and not the builder summary
documentation plan and traceability recorded; docs committed on the job branch
Documentation Quality Gate (links, snippets, diagrams, readability, coverage) plus independent documentation reviewer
control plane pushes the branch and opens a draft pull request with the evidence manifest; verifies the PR exists and the body carries the manifest hash
human decision: approve, reject, rework, pause or cancel
not implemented; disabled by default; requires per-repository policy and final re-validation after merge-base sync

rework_routes.note: clarify loop; unresolved product decisions go to a human
the builder receives the gate reports, not a summary
findings are deduplicated before the builder sees them; applies to defect classes code_behavior and documentation, see defect_routing
the documentation exposed a code or behavior mismatch
human instructions are authorized input but still untrusted text; the baseline route, see human_rework_routes for the full set

defect_routing.description: How the defect classes of a reviewer's findings route a CHANGES_REQUIRED verdict. Only the four stages with an independent reviewer use it; the other gates are deterministic and use the single route in rework_routes. The class is taken from the findings that justify the verdict (severity blocker, high or medium). When classes differ, the first in precedence wins, so a decision that needs a person is never hidden behind an easier fix. A deterministic failure at DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW has no reviewer class and counts as documentation. 'rework' means the route in rework_routes (DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW picks its row by class). 'human' means gate_needs_human (S10): the stage run waits for a person, and no automatic rework happens.

human_rework_routes.description: Where a person may send rework from a stage run that waits for a human or is blocked (S15). The person names the target. A target is an agent-produced stage at or before the waiting stage: ARCHITECTURE, TASK_PLANNING, IMPLEMENTATION or DOCUMENTING. SPECIFICATION is a target only from SPECIFICATION itself, because revising a frozen specification needs the spec adapter's revision method (ADR 0006), which is not proven in Slice 1. INTAKE, REPOSITORY_INTELLIGENCE and DOMAIN_DISCOVERY have no human rework route; a person answers, approves or rejects there. Each round is charged to the count of its target: the specification count for SPECIFICATION, the design count for ARCHITECTURE and TASK_PLANNING, the code count for IMPLEMENTATION and the documentation count for DOCUMENTING (ADR 0023), and the cap of two applies to each.

invalidation_rules.when: SPECIFICATION produces a new approved spec version
TASK_PLANNING produces a new plan version

invalidation_rules.note: gate_integrity.invalidated_by: new_commit and rebase. A rebase writes new commits, so it counts as a new commit.

invalidation_rules.when: DOCUMENTING produces a new documentation commit
The source request is edited after the intake snapshot
invalidation_rules.note: An external change, so the intake run is superseded too. The new intake run asks for re-authorization before any agent reads the new text (NT-AUTHZ-05).

invalidation_rules.when: REPOSITORY_INTELLIGENCE produces a new repository map
invalidation_rules.note: The specification consumed the map and the baseline.

invalidation_rules.when: A value bound to gate evidence changes
invalidation_rules.note: The values are the base commit, the gate definition hash, the policy hash and the sandbox image digest (gate_integrity.evidence_binding). gate_integrity.invalidated_by: base_moved, policy_change and image_change. Checked at two points, before DELIVERY pushes and when an approval is recorded. DOCUMENTING is not superseded, because the documentation text did not change.

assurance_levels.description: Claims about how far the work has been verified. Each is recorded as evidence ledger entries and derived from them. They are not Job states and they are not ordered: VERIFIED_ON_DEVICE does not imply VERIFIED_IN_SIMULATOR.

requires_evidence: commit hash on the job branch
trusted gate reports PASSED in a fresh sandbox
acceptance scenario evidence for every requirement
levels.note: Added for software that has no simulator or device. Not named in the master prompt; listed in the open questions.

requires_evidence: acceptance results from a simulator or emulator run, with the simulator version
acceptance results from a physical device run, with device identity
paper-trading results over the period required by the profile
every mandatory gate of every active domain profile PASSED
no open blocker without a disposition

release_states.description: A second, independent axis for delivery after approval. Not implemented in Slice 1: the factory stops at APPROVED and a human merges.

invariants.statement: Only the engine writes a status. A worker or an agent can request a transition but cannot perform one.
enforced_by: workflow use cases are the only callers of the repository write methods
verified_by: property test: random command sequences never reach a state outside the tables
storage integration test: a stale version is rejected

invariants.statement: A transition not listed in this file is rejected with a typed error and leaves the stored state unchanged.
verified_by: conformance test: the cross product of states and events minus this table is rejected

invariants.statement: A stage run is PASSED only when the gate decision and its evidence are persisted in the same transaction as the status change.
verified_by: integration test: failure injected after the status write rolls back the status

invariants.statement: A terminal stage run is never edited. Rework and supersession create or mark runs; they do not reopen them.
verified_by: database test: UPDATE of a terminal row fails

invariants.statement: A write from a worker whose lease epoch is older than the stored epoch is rejected, whatever it contains.
verified_by: integration test: zombie worker write after LEASE_LOST is rejected

invariants.statement: A mandatory gate that did not run is BLOCKED. Missing execution is never converted to PASSED.
verified_by: schema invalid example; gate evaluator test with the tool removed

invariants.statement: An override of a BLOCK never creates an assurance level claim and is never allowed for a mandatory gate of an active domain profile.
verified_by: engine test with a profile whose mandatory tool is absent

invariants.statement: Evidence recorded by a fake adapter is accepted only when the job execution mode is test, and never supports an assurance level.
verified_by: schema invalid example; engine test in production mode with a fake adapter

invariants.statement: Superseding a stage run invalidates its ledger entries by appending new entries. Existing entries are never changed.
enforced_by: append-only ledger with no UPDATE or DELETE privilege
verified_by: database test: UPDATE and DELETE on the ledger fail

invariants.statement: The number of attempts per stage run (counted since the last human answer) and rework rounds per job are bounded by policy (default: three attempts, two rework rounds on each of the specification, design, code and documentation counts, and two repairs after an invalid output). Exhaustion, including a budget limit, escalates to a human; it does not loop, and it does not fail the stage run.
verified_by: engine test with an always-failing fake runtime reaches WAITING_FOR_HUMAN in a bounded number of steps
domain test: BUDGET_EXHAUSTED and an exhausted attempt limit choose S07, never S06

invariants.statement: DOCUMENTING and DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW run after REVIEW has passed and before DELIVERY and APPROVAL. A new implementation commit supersedes them.
enforced_by: pipeline requires and invalidation_rules in this file
verified_by: engine test: a rework after DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW supersedes both documentation runs
